entities.summary: Kasım Ağa Mosque is a Byzantine building converted into a mosque by the Ottomans in Istanbul, Turkey. Neither surveying during the last restoration nor medieval sources have made it possible to find a satisfactory answer as to its origin and possible dedication. It is probable that the small building was part of the Byzantine complex and monastery whose main church was the building known in Ottoman era as the Odalar Mosque, whose dedication is also uncertain. The edifice is a minor example of Byzantine architecture in Constantinople. Kasım Ağa Mosque, Istanbul is a mosque in Asia. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a minor example of Byzantine architecture in Constantinople, the Kasım Ağa Mosque played a role in the Ottoman Empire's conversion of existing Christian buildings into mosques. Its significance lies in its representation of the complex and dynamic cultural exchange between Eastern Orthodox Christianity and Islam during the Ottoman period.
